about.explain: Explains a wrong answer under the exercise (“Why is this wrong?”): what the mistake is and the rule behind it, in your language.
about.tutor: The lesson's tutor: answers your questions about the lesson, its words and grammar, and explains — hints first for the exercise on screen. Practice is in the lesson's AI steps.
about.tutorSection: The tutor on its own, in the Tutor section: answers whatever you ask outside a lesson — a grammar question, a text to go through, a conversation to practise — knowing what you have met in your courses.
about.writingTask: Sets the task of “Write it yourself”: a situation from the lesson with three points to cover, its length by the course's level, as a writing exam at that level sets one. Asked once per task.
about.writing: Checks a short text written on the task of “Write it yourself”: each point covered or not, at most three corrections, the criteria of the course's level (task, communication, accuracy), a model text and feedback.
about.speaking: Checks an answer you said aloud (what the recogniser heard) against the question and the course's answer, when you press “Check with AI”.
about.exam: Rates a written answer of an exam by the exam's own criteria: a level of each with its reason, and what would score more. Nothing counts until you take or change it.
about.conversation: Holds a speaking part of an exam: plays the examiner and the other candidate, as the part prescribes, line by line with you; it never helps or corrects. Rated afterwards by the part's criteria.
about.sceneSetup: Starts a dialogue: from the lesson's goals and what you know, invents the situation, who you talk to, your goal card and what only your partner knows — which you must ask for. Asked once per dialogue.
about.scene: Plays your partner: answers each line you say (as the recogniser heard it) or type, says whether it was understood and fits, corrects at most two mistakes in it, gives a translation and ticks off your goals.
about.examples: Writes three to five example sentences for each word of a deck that has none of its own, five words at a time (Review → Decks, “Make examples”), with words you know where it can and the new ones translated.
about.sceneSummary: Sums up a dialogue once it is over: the one or two corrections that matter most, each with your line said well, and a word of feedback.
about.understanding: Writes a short text in the language you learn from the words you know — a dialogue or an announcement to listen to, or a menu or a notice to read — with questions as exams ask them (true/false, a/b/c, numbers). Your answers are checked by the app, not by the model.
about.understandingCheck: Reads the text again and answers its own questions from the text alone: a question it answers otherwise, or finds unclear, is left out.
about.mistakes: Goes over a pass's mistakes by type: each type's wrong parts only (what you gave, what is right, the words around it), a short explanation, and two or three new items of the type from words you know. Your answers are checked by the app, not by the model.

guide.title: How review works
guide.curveAlt: Three forgetting curves, each flatter than the one before
guide.curveCaption: Memory fades unless it is used: each review at the edge of forgetting makes the curve flatter, so the next one can wait longer.

method.title: Spaced repetition
method.text: Each card comes back just before you would forget it. The intervals grow with every good answer: minutes, then days, weeks, months. The idea goes back to Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve (1885).

recall.title: Remember first, then look
recall.text: Try to recall the answer before you show it. The effort of recalling is what strengthens memory — reading the answer again does far less. Then rate yourself honestly.

again.name: Again
again.text: not remembered, or wrong: the card comes back in a minute

hard.name: Hard
hard.text: remembered with effort: a shorter interval

good.name: Good
good.text: remembered: the usual choice (Space or Enter)

easy.name: Easy
easy.text: too easy: it comes back much later

counts.title: The three numbers
counts.text: New cards still to learn today, cards in learning (coming back within minutes), and cards due for review. The one underlined is where the card on screen comes from. "Answers to go" estimates how many answers finish the session if each is Good.

production.name: Card 2
production.text: the meaning → the word (speaking); it comes after card 1

listening.name: Card 3
listening.text: the word heard → what it means (listening)

bury.name: Bury (- or =)
bury.text: not today: the card or the whole word comes back tomorrow

suspend.name: Suspend (@ or !)
suspend.text: out of review until you bring it back — a word you know or do not need

flag.name: Flags (Ctrl+1–7)
flag.text: colour marks to find cards later in My words

mark.name: Mark (*)
mark.text: a star on the word, to come back to it

keys.title: Keys
keys.text: Space or Enter shows the answer, then rates Good; 1–4 rate; U or Ctrl+Z takes the last answer back; R replays.

fsrs.title: FSRS
fsrs.text: The schedule is FSRS, an open spaced-repetition model: it estimates how stable each memory is and when you would forget it, aiming at your desired retention (90% by default). The limits, the retention and the card types are in Settings.

schedule.title: Steps and the day
schedule.steps: A new card answered Good comes back after 10 minutes (after Again, in a minute), then after days; a forgotten one after 10 minutes, and its interval grows again.
schedule.day: A new day starts at {time}: reviews between midnight and then count for the day before.
schedule.limit: New cards count against the maximum reviews: once it is reached, no new cards are shown that day.

reviewSettings.intro: Spaced repetition of your cards: a word comes back when you are about to forget it. The defaults suit most learners.
reviewSettings.limitsHint: A word with two card types is two new cards. Each new card brings about 5–10 reviews in its first month.
reviewSettings.retentionHint: How likely you still remember a card when it comes back. Higher means more reviews; 90% by default.
reviewSettings.faces: Card types of a new word
reviewSettings.facesHint: Which cards a new word gets. Words that have cards keep theirs.

sources.title: Sources and checks
sources.statement: Every question, picture, recording and answer here was read from the documents below by the importer on this computer — none written by hand or by a model — and checked as listed. A mock exam asks the same tasks and scores them by the same rules as the official model test; it shows how ready you are, not what the real exam will give.

suggest.text: Go through a text with me

ask.grammar: I have a grammar question. Ask me what it is, then explain it briefly with examples from what I have learnt.

ask.conversation: Let's practise a conversation. Suggest an everyday situation from what I have learnt, then start with one line and wait for my answer; correct my mistakes as we go.
